newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast spot gasoline ease Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast spot gasoline ease Tuesday.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot wholesale gasoline prices eased Tuesday, with trade thin most of the day as players waited for inventory reports from the American Petroleum Institute (API), traders said.
On the NYMEX, June unleaded gasoline rose a slight 0.18 cents a barrel to $65.39 a barrel, while crude oil dropped 0.40 cents a gallon to $21.19 cents a gallon.
West Coast gasoline stocks fell 835,000 barrels on the week to 29.6 million, API said.
++ GASOLINE: Traders pegged offers for May CARB unleaded gasoline at 61.50 cents a gallon in Los Angeles, down one cent from Monday.
Traders said sellers were trying to fix ships to move gasoline east, where shipments can fetch better prices than the weak West Coast market.
Bids for conventional grade unleaded fell one cent to 58.50 cents.
++ DISTILLATES: Trade shifted to June shipments, with offers for CARB diesel in L.A. at 62.50/63.50 cents.
